title: Spectral / power-law analysis of activation probes for jailbreak detection robustness across architectures

original_idea.body:
# Spectral / power-law analysis of activation probes for jailbreak detection robustness across architectures

**Problem:** Activation-probe jailbreak detectors are reported as cheap and effective, but we don't know how the probe direction's geometry varies across model families, or whether a probe trained on one architecture transfers — limiting reuse.

**Direction:** Apply tools from spectral analysis / signal processing. Train simple linear probes for 'harmful-intent' on hidden states of several small open models, then analyze the spectral/cosine geometry of the learned directions and how harmful vs. benign activations separate along principal components. Test cross-model probe transfer and whether a low-rank shared subspace exists. Quantify transfer accuracy vs. layer.

**Why it matters:** Establishes whether cheap activation probes are portable across open models (a replication gap), informing whether the community can share one probe rather than retrain per model. Linear probing only; fits 30h and consumer GPU.

**Relevant context:** Grounded in landscape's activation-based jailbreak detection result and its replication-gap call ('replicate on different model families'). Source subfield: signal processing / spectral analysis. Target subfield: adversarial_robustness, mechanistic_interpretability.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: probe portability informs reusable jailbreak detection, but the catastrophic-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: linear probing plus PCA/cosine analysis across small models, single GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (cross-model transfer accuracy vs layer), few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: open models, replication-flavored, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Linear probing on small open models, consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Probe transfer is a flagged replication gap; the spectral-geometry angle may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Probe-transfer replication exists; spectral framing plausibly partly open.
